problem: Existing navigation agents are each designed and trained for one task (image-, audio-, object-goal, vision-language), and no dataset supports these tasks in one standardized continuous audiovisual environment, so a single multitask navigation agent has been out of reach.
motivation: Humans learn multiple tasks in parallel and integrate multiple senses, while MTRL for visually rich embodied navigation is largely unexplored. Cross-task knowledge sharing could improve performance, generalization and model size, but it needs a unified benchmark and a unified agent design.
key_idea: Cast four navigation tasks as one parse-and-query process: the target, augmented with all four learnable task embeddings, is parsed online into several goal vectors that query the episodic history through a partly shared Transformer decoder.
insight: Adding all four task embeddings to the target description (including those of other tasks) helps: augmented G beats target-only 25.3/18.7 vs 23.1/17.2 AGN SR (seen/unseen). A shared-trunk planner (2 shared + 2 private layers) beats fully separate or fully shared decoders. Adding more tasks improves AGN unseen SR 15.4→16.1→17.3→18.7 and VLN 14.1→14.9→15.5→16.3, and the multitask model costs 31M params vs 101M for four single-task models. Gains from multitask training are larger for VIENNA than for Seq2Seq.
method: VXN dataset: converts SoundSpaces audio-goal, R2R VLN, Habitat ImageNav and ObjectNav (21 categories) into one continuous MP3D/Habitat setup with 360° RGBD and binaural audio, using BRIR interpolation for continuous audio; 9.6M train episodes; 1 m success radius, 500-step limit.

Episodic Encoder: ResNet50 RGB/depth encoders and an audio CNN encode 12 panoramic sub-views; target-guided cross-attention plus two self-attention MSI blocks give per-step observation tokens, which are combined with the previous action into navigation tokens and encoded by a 4-block causal Transformer over the full episode history.

Target Parser: goal image, sound, class tag or instruction (bi-LSTM) is embedded, padded to N_G, and summed with learnable task embeddings for all four tasks (zeros for the inactive ones) to form augmented G; an N=5-head attention conditioned on the pooled history yields time-varying goal embeddings Q_t.

Multitask Planner: a 4-layer Transformer decoder in which Q_t queries the history; the first 2 layers are shared across tasks and the last 2 are task-private; a softmax over 12 sub-view directions plus STOP gives the action.

MDPPO training: multitask distributed PPO with four client workers, each holding four task-specific agent copies to balance the 10.8K VLN episodes against millions for the other tasks; reward = success 2.5 + geodesic progress + slack −1e-3 + voxel exploration bonus.
Training details: 32 RTX 2080 GPUs, 180M frames (4,608 GPU hours), AdamW lr 2.5e-4, d=512, greedy action selection.

setting.backbone: VIENNA: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 (RGB), modified ResNet50 (depth), audio CNN, bi-LSTM, Transformer encoder-decoder, trained end-to-end with RL (MDPPO)
setting.training_data: VXN train: 9.6M episodes over 58 MP3D environments (2.0M audio-goal, 10,819 VLN, 2.6M object-goal, 5.0M image-goal); 180M frames; RL, no extra data
setting.observation: 360° panoramic RGB (12x224x224) + depth (12x256x256) + binaural audio spectrogram (12 directions), no GPS/compass
setting.action_space: panoramic: choose one of 12 sub-view directions and move 0.25 m, or STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat with SoundSpaces audio (continuous audio rendering), Matterport3D scenes

numbers.backbone: VIENNA multitask (31M, one model for four tasks)
numbers.extra: 1 m success radius, 500-step limit; RL-trained on VXN

numbers_note: Results are on the new VXN benchmark (not standard R2R/ObjectNav benchmarks), so they are labeled other:VXN-*; baselines were re-trained or re-evaluated under VXN's 1 m success criterion.
results: On VXN, the single multitask VIENNA beats its single-task version on all four tasks (e.g., VLN val-unseen SR 16.3 vs 14.3; AGN 18.7 vs 14.3). It also beats the task-specific baselines (Krantz et al. VLN-CE 11.0 SR, Chen et al. 13.1, Zhu et al. 12.0, Chaplot et al. 17.6 on unseen) with roughly a quarter of the parameters of four separate models.
limitations: Absolute success rates are low, especially on unseen environments (14-19% SR), leaving the tasks far from solved.
Evaluated only in simulation on MP3D, with heavy training cost (32 GPUs, 4,608 GPU hours); the VLN data is small (10.8K episodes) and the tasks share the same scene set.
Ablations cover only AGN and VLN; the test split is not used; baselines were re-trained or re-evaluated under different conditions.
